name: 1923 - GEC - Chenard Walcker 2l Tourisme - S2.0
description:
CHENARD & WALCKER
------------------------------------------------------------
Car: Chenard & Walcker 2L Tourisme
Origin: France
Year: 1923
Class: 2.0L Touring Class (S2.0)
------------------------------------------------------------
3D Model: Marguek
------------------------------------------------------------
description:

The Chenard & Walcker 2L Tourisme was one of the key entries fielded by Chenard & Walcker during the inaugural 24 Hours of Le Mans. Built to comply with the Touring category regulations, the car emphasized reliability, efficiency, and road-going practicality rather than outright speed. Its 2.0-liter inline engine was modest in output but engineered to sustain long-distance endurance without major mechanical stress—an essential trait for a race that was still an unknown challenge at the time.

The chassis and bodywork followed a fairly conventional touring layout, featuring full fenders, lighting equipment, and a more “road car” silhouette compared to the stripped-down racers of later decades. This adherence to production-based design reflected the early philosophy of Le Mans: proving the durability of cars customers could actually buy. The 2L Tourisme embodied this ethos almost perfectly.

During the race, the car demonstrated impressive consistency. While it lacked the outright pace of larger-engined competitors, its steady lap times and mechanical resilience allowed it to remain competitive over the full 24-hour duration. In an era where many cars failed to finish due to mechanical breakdowns, simply completing the race was a significant achievement—and the 2L Tourisme did so with commendable stability.

Its performance contributed to the overall dominance of Chenard & Walcker in the 1923 event, reinforcing the brand’s reputation for engineering robustness. Though overshadowed by its larger sibling in outright results, the 2L Tourisme played a crucial supporting role in showcasing the manufacturer’s range and capability.

------------------------------------------------------------
fun fact:

The 2L Tourisme closely resembled a normal road car of its time; meaning, in theory, you could drive something very similar to a Le Mans competitor straight off a dealership floor in 1923.
